statement.en: This level is set on the Yukon River at Whitehorse, the capital of Yukon. Discover Canada says the Gold Rush of the 1890s brought thousands of miners to the Yukon, and that mining is still a big part of the economy. The White Pass and Yukon Railway reached Whitehorse from Skagway, in neighbouring Alaska, in 1900.
statement.fr: Ce niveau se déroule au bord du fleuve Yukon, à Whitehorse, la capitale du Yukon. Discover Canada dit que la ruée vers l'or des années 1890 a amené des milliers de mineurs au Yukon, et que l'exploitation minière compte encore beaucoup dans l'économie. Le chemin de fer White Pass and Yukon a atteint Whitehorse depuis Skagway, en Alaska voisine, en 1900.

source.quote: The White Pass and Yukon Railway opened from Skagway in neighbouring Alaska to the territorial capital, Whitehorse in 1900

verification.evidence: KDFN’s Traditional Territory encompasses the Yukon’s capital and economic heartland, the City of Whitehorse. Approximately 75 per cent of Yukon’s population lives on KDFN Traditional Territory. … We acknowledge the Tagish Kwan as the original people who live and occupy the lands that define our Traditional Territory, alongside the headwaters of Chu Níikwän (today, the Yukon River). Our people have been here for millennia.

blurb.en: The Northwest Territories, Nunavut and Yukon hold a third of Canada's land. Very few people live across all that space.
blurb.fr: Les Territoires du Nord-Ouest, le Nunavut et le Yukon occupent le tiers des terres du Canada. Très peu de gens vivent dans cet immense espace.

source.quote: The Northwest Territories, Nunavut and Yukon contain one-third of Canada's land mass but have a population of only 100,000.

verification.evidence: The Northwest Territories, Nunavut and Yukon contain one-third of Canada’s land mass but have a population of only 100,000.

name.fr: Vapeur à roue arrière du Yukon

blurb.en: People call the North the Land of the Midnight Sun. At midsummer the sky can stay bright for a full 24 hours. Winter does the opposite: the sun drops out of sight and three months pass in the dark. Tundra covers much of the region — a huge stony Arctic plain where the ground never thaws and trees cannot grow.
blurb.fr: On appelle le Nord le pays du soleil de minuit. Au cœur de l'été, le ciel peut rester clair pendant 24 heures d'affilée. L'hiver fait le contraire : le soleil disparaît de la vue et trois mois s'écoulent dans la noirceur. La toundra couvre une grande partie de la région — une immense plaine rocheuse de l'Arctique où le sol ne dégèle jamais et où les arbres ne poussent pas.

source.quote: The North is often referred to as the “Land of the Midnight Sun” because at the height of summer, daylight can last up to 24 hours. In winter, the sun disappears and darkness sets in for three months. The Northern territories have long cold winters and short cool summers. Much of the North is made up of tundra, the vast rocky Arctic plain. Because of the cold Arctic climate, there are no trees on the tundra and the soil is permanently frozen.

blurb.en: Thousands of miners came to the Yukon in the Gold Rush of the 1890s. Mining is still a big part of the territory's economy.
blurb.fr: Des milliers de mineurs sont venus au Yukon pendant la ruée vers l'or des années 1890. L'exploitation minière demeure une grande part de l'économie du territoire.

source.quote: Thousands of miners came to the Yukon during the Gold Rush of the 1890s, as celebrated in the poetry of Robert W. Service. Mining remains a significant part of the economy.
